newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-SIEMERINK BEATS BOETSCH FOR PLACE IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SIEMERINK BEATS BOETSCH FOR PLACE IN FINAL.

text.p: Jan Siemerink of the Netherlands booked a place in the final of the $800,000 CA Trophy on Saturday by knocking out Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch 7-6 (9-7) 6-4.
Siemerink will contest his second final on the indoor hardcourt at Vienna's Stadthalle, after losing to Germany's Michael Stich in straight sets in 1991.
The Dutchman, currently ranked 36th in the world, has made seven appearances here and reached the quarter-finals five times.
"I have no idea why I always play so well here," he said. "When I make my schedule I always try to stick with tournaments where I know I always do well."
Siemerink had a slow start in the match, failing to convert five break points and needing his seventh set point to clinch the first set.
"In the first set I had a lot of chances I couldn't make and when he (Boetsch) had a set point, I got very nervous. It was a crucial set.

"I was a bit tired today after the match against Stefan (Edberg) yesterday. I felt a bit slower than on other days," said Siemerink, who on Friday defeated the sentimental favourite from Sweden in three sets.
Siemerink profited from a double fault from Boetsch for a quick break in the second set's opening game which was followed by another break four games later.
